about.title: About
about.intro: How the site measures the real length of a masechet, and what the numbers can and cannot tell.

unit.title: The unit: full dafim
unit.definition: Take one text alone, for example the Gemara, and imagine it printed with nothing else around it, filling the whole text body of each page. The number of dafim it would fill is its length in full dafim. One full daf is two complete text bodies (both amudim) of that single text.
unit.example: {tractate} has {printed} printed dafim, but its Gemara alone would fill {main} full dafim: {share} of its text body. The rest is Rashi, Tosafot, headings and spacing.
unit.units: In the preferences you can also show full amudim (half a full daf) or the share of the text body in percent.

method.title: How it is measured
method.stepPdf: The pages of the Vilna Shas are read from the PDFs published by Shas.org.
method.stepMatch: Each line of text on the page is matched against the texts of Sefaria and Wikisource, to know whether it belongs to the Gemara, Rashi, Tosafot or another commentary.
method.stepArea: For each text, the area of its line boxes is added up and divided by the text body fitted on the masechet's pages. This gives the share of each amud that the text fills.
method.stepTotal: These shares are added up over the masechet and divided by two to get full dafim.
method.notCalculatedSmall: The commentaries of Shekalim, Kinnim, Tamid and Middos.

caveats.title: Caveats
caveats.estimate: Every value is an automatic estimate. It has not been checked by hand.
caveats.frames: Each masechet has its own fitted text frame, so comparisons between masechtot are approximate.
caveats.unknown: "Not calculated" means unknown, never zero. Unknown values are never added into a total.
